fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Nighttime conspicuity of a HAWK display against competing background elements is a substantive final-design-stage safety issue directly affecting drivers' ability to stop for crossing pedestrians.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (driver confusion from competing night-time background elements at this site) is supported by a verbatim quote under EV-US-001, exceeding registry-id-only citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern with no normative_basis_note, keeping it distinct from compliance questions per FHWA RSA semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Recommendation is specific to the named intersection, actionable at final design, and reflects a viable standard treatment (retroreflective border on the signal head).
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians—the VRUs exposed if drivers misread or detect the beacon late—are explicitly identified in road_users and linked to the driver-conspicuity mechanism.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance adequacy for slower walkers at signalized/HAWK crossings is a classic final-design-stage safety check, and the sites are flagged as high pedestrian/bicycle collision locations, making the concern substantive.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-US-016 provides a verbatim quote ('The pedestrian clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians.') directly supporting the pivotal claim, tied to the recorded case-study issue for these exact sites.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as an RSA safety concern (verify design assumption/walking speed) rather than a MUTCD compliance assertion, keeping the categorical distinction intact under FHWA audit semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: names all six HAWK sites, the action (reprogramme clearance intervals), and the method (reduced assumed walking speed), all feasible before signal deployment at final design.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and specifically elderly pedestrians are named road users and the explicit focus of both scenario and statement, so vulnerable-user impacts are fully considered.
